title: Retrospective analysis of transarterial radioembolization (TARE) in hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tumors (NET) at University Hospital Essen
summary:
Project title, version number, version date
Project title: Retrospective analysis of transarterial radioembolization (TARE) in hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tumors (NET) at University Hospital Essen
Version: 1.0
Date: 22 August 2025

Responsibilities
Principal Investigator:
Dr. med. univ. Dr. med. Thomas Dertnig
Institute of Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology and Neuroradiology
University Hospital Essen
Hufelandstr. 55, 45147 Essen, Germany
E-Mail: Thomas.Dertnig@uk-essen.de
Phone: +49 (0)201 723 82847
Institutions:
University Medicine Essen
Registration according to the Declaration of Helsinki:
Planned (purely retrospective, anonymized evaluation).

Data sources
Imaging datasets (CT, MRI, SPECT/PET) and reports from PACS and RIS of the Institute of Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology and Neuroradiology
Documentation from inpatient and outpatient stays related to TARE treatments
Laboratory values, tumor board protocols, interventional reports
Study period: 01 January 2000 to 01 August 2025
Patient cohort: approx. 50 patients with histologically confirmed hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tumors (NET) and liver-dominant metastases who underwent TARE
Approval of the hospital management: to be attached via Form 7

Biometry
Complete inclusion of all eligible cases within the study period
Expected sample size: approx. 50 patients
No formal sample size calculation (retrospective, exploratory)
Analyses:
Descriptive statistics
Kaplan-Meier curves for OS and PFS
Comparison of hormonal parameters pre- and post-treatment
Univariate and, if applicable, multivariate analyses of prognostic factors

Data management & data protection
Legal basis: Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (legitimate interest in research), § 27 BDSG
Retrospective, fully anonymized data evaluation
Storage: encrypted on internal hospital servers, access limited to the study team
No transfer to third parties without separate approval
No possibility of patient re-identification
conditions: Histologically confirmed hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tumor (NET)  (C7B.02 — Secondary neuroendocrine tumor of liver)
